summary: Kpacku's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Demo compo at DiHalt 2026 Summer, with code and graphics by Tutty, concept and code by Trefi, and music by C-jeff and Riskej.
why: A first place in the DiHalt 2026 Summer demo competition, and it was well received on Pouët.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 48K demo, an 8-bit lyric video for Darude's Sandstorm, with code, music and graphics by Gasman and graphics by rc55. It came second in Realtime Wild at Outline 2017.
why: A karaoke-style joke prod that placed second in the Realtime Wild compo at Outline 2017, done on a stock 48K Spectrum.

summary: A ZX Spectrum Enhanced demo by Hacker VBI that won the ZX Spectrum Enhanced Demo compo at 3BM OpenAir 2014.
why: It took first place in its compo at 3BM OpenAir 2014, which makes it a good look at what Hacker VBI could do on the extended Spectrum platforms.

summary: A Game Boy Color demo by Dual Crew Shining from 2000, with code by Sasq, graphics by Vodka, music by Laxity and a DCS logo by Iridon. The video is filmed on a real Game Boy Color.
why: No compo placing or comments to go on, but it's a Game Boy Color demo from a group whose credits include Laxity on music, and the capture shows it running on original hardware.
highlights: filmed on a real Game Boy Color

summary: A 32-byte-category Atari 8-bit intro by JAC!, released in May 2011. The video title gives its actual size as 23 bytes.
why: An example of how much can be squeezed from a couple of dozen bytes on the Atari. It's tagged as a glitch and noise piece, and was well received on Pouët.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K intro from RET and Darklite, code by Neon and music by Ref, that came 9th in the Demo compo at Outline 2023. A big wavy scroller runs across a starfield beneath a static credits screen.
why: Tagged as a demake: the on-screen credits say the original intro was by Dan & Mat, and this brings it to the Spectrum for Outline 2023.

summary: An Oric 40k intro by Dbug of NeXT and Defence Force, made for the C64 Times Revisited compo at STNICCC 2000, where it took first place.
why: It won its compo at STNICCC 2000, an Oric entry coming out on top in a competition themed around revisiting the C64.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Busy and Noro that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Demobit 1995.
why: A compo winner from Demobit 1995, tagged for its use of the Spectrum's multicolour mode, which gets past the machine's usual attribute-colour limits.

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2021.
why: A compo winner at one of the main Russian-speaking scene parties, and well received on Pouët.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by Ilmenit (code) and stRing (music) that placed second in the 256b intro compo at Decrunch 2020. It shows a rotating spiral galaxy against a starfield.
why: It was nominated for Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2021, and it fits both visuals and sound into 256 bytes. The source code is available.

summary: Noice's demo for the TI-83 graphing calculator, filmed on the device itself, which placed 2nd in the wild demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2002.
why: A calculator demo that took second place in a wild compo at Mekka & Symposium, and an early example of the TI-8x scene showing up at a major European party.

summary: A 16K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Osmium Path, with code by Optimus and graphics and music by Ham. It placed 4th in the Combined Demo compo at Demosplash 2024.
why: A recent example of a size-limited CPC intro from Optimus and Ham that held its own in a mixed-platform demo compo at Demosplash 2024.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Dalthon of Joker that won the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2022.
why: It took first place in its size-limited compo at DiHalt 2022, a neat example of what fits into 256 bytes on a stock Spectrum.

summary: Booze Design's single-file C64 demo for a 512K REU memory expansion, which won the C64 demo compo at The REU Compo 2015. Code by HCL and Ruk, graphics and music by Dane, charset by Valsary.
why: Sceners saw it as the first demo to push the REU really hard, with record-breaking screens packed into about five minutes. Its sideborder tricks even exposed gaps in REU emulation and in how people thought the hardware behaved.

quote.text: WOW, thats how one utilizes REU :) Great production. And all that in a single PRG.

summary: Oxyron's C64 demo that won the Oldschool demo compo at Nordlicht 2014, built around a Chuck Rock-style band scene with a rock soundtrack by Celticdesign, sampled drums and a fast custom loader by Bitbreaker.
why: Sceners singled out the full-frame character animation, the mix of samples and SID, a catchy tune they rated above the original game music, and a loader quick enough to draw comment.

quote.text: Nice little prod. Full frame char animation rocked the most for me! :)

summary: Origo Dreamline's three-part C64 scroller demo that won the C64 demo compo at Horizon Easter Party 1990, with large colourful scrolling fonts, a shiny logo and a Star Wars scroller end part.
why: Sceners remember the reaction at Horizon 1990 and single out the colours above all: a logo that showed the C64 could look that shiny, an early AFLI picture, the big three-colour scrolling font, and music by Mixer and Zardax.

quote.text: First time I saw that logo my jaw hit the floor; I had no idea the hardware was capable of anything that shiny.

summary: Pulpo Corrosivo's Amstrad CPC demo, coded and directed by Toms with music by Targhan, which placed 6th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2019.
why: A Revision oldskool compo entry from the CPC, with textured graphics from Beb and Barjack and logos and a picture by rexbeng. Tagged for its tunnel and rubber-vector effects.

summary: Megastyle's 1993 Commodore 64 demo, also known as Digital Messiah: a dark, atmospheric piece told in separate chapters, with large drawn pictures, a rune font and an endscroller.
why: Sceners call it an overlooked classic that chose style and concept over technical showing-off. They single out the atmosphere, the chaptered design and the metal SID soundtrack, though several grumble about the slow loader.

quote.text: These guys went for style and a concept, not a tech demo. I love what they did and like a few others they prove you don't always need some tech revolution to impress.

summary: Singular's C64 invitation, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at QBParty 2017. A pixelled city picture by Poison and Leon opens it, then a 3D letter scroller glides over an isometric grid of waving blocks.
why: Sceners liked the scroller and the waving block routine, and one admitted to having no clue how the effect is done. Soci explained that the letters' perspective was switched off in Blender to match the isometric background.

quote.text: I really like the scroller and the waving block routine very much!

summary: Fit's PETSCII demo for the C64, with a Plus/4 version too, that won the C64 demo compo at Zoo 2013. Code by Dr. TerrorZ and Marq, graphics by Dr. TerrorZ, music by Yzi.
why: Sceners praise its character-mode art and animation, the goth girl band and the vertical scroller with a shadow, all carried by Yzi's tune. Some still count it among their favourite PETSCII pieces years later.

quote.text: Awesome PETSCII demo, with brilliant PETSCII art!

summary: A small one-file C64 demo by Gheymaid Inc., placed 8th in the 8-bit demo compo at Oxyron Party 2008. Code and charsets by Motion, a picture by Helm and music by Psycho8580.
why: Sceners single out the moody soundtrack, the lovely charsets and Helm's picture, which one commenter said has a mid-80s Compunet feel. Its appeal is atmosphere rather than technical show.

quote.text: Beautiful little production here...great music and graphics create a wonderful atmosphere

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by MaPa (code) and PG (music) that won the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2017. Rows of solid-shaded 3D cubes spin in a grid of colourful panels.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2017 that fits rotating filled cubes and a soundtrack into a single kilobyte.

summary: Censor Design's Matrix-themed C64 demo, third in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2013, with a borderless Matrix character effect, a plasma, a Trinity picture and a tribute part to Mogwai.
why: Sceners single out the Matrix character effect spilling into the side border, an unusually good-looking 8x8 plasma and Prowler's end picture. The Mogwai part, set to an old Future Freak tune, touched many viewers.

quote.text: It's also amazing that new ways to exploit the hardware can still be found in 2013.

summary: Single-effect C64 demo by Panoramic Designs and Prosonix, code by Bjørn Røstøen and music by Stein Pedersen, released as part 2 of the Pandemoniac series. It placed 3rd in the C64 Demo compo at Datastorm 2017 Summer.
why: Sceners call it one of the prettiest twister-type effects on the C64, praising how smooth and mesmerising the swirl is and how well Stein Pedersen's tune sets the mood. Several wished it had been part of a bigger demo.

quote.text: One of the prettiest twister-type effects on c-64.

summary: An MSX demo by Lieves!Tuore, with code by Marq, music by Yzi and graphics by Manu. It placed 9th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2013.
why: A modern MSX production from a Finnish-scene group, entered at Revision 2013. It's worth a look for its blocky, brightly coloured character-grid visuals.

summary: Aids' Atari 8-bit demo from 1999, coded by MacGyver with music by Teque and Ce-Pumpkin, which won the demo competition at Last Party 1999.
why: A compo winner from the late-1990s Polish Atari scene. Its credits screen is candid, with MacGyver writing that only the scroller is the reason for his pride.
highlights: scroller the coder was proud of

summary: A C16/Plus 4 tribute demo by Monarchy, coded by Csio, which won the demo compo at Árok 2011. Its German title translates as "He passed away peacefully".
why: It won its compo at Árok 2011 and is a memorial piece rather than a straight effects show, which makes it a less common kind of Plus 4 demo.

summary: A C64 4K intro by AEG of Smash Designs and Axis of Oxyron, placed third in the C64 4K compo at Breakpoint 2003: a full-screen rotozoomer over a tiled texture of shaded spheres.
why: The authors claimed a full-screen 2x2-pixel rotozoomer at 25 fps had never been done before, and sceners still puzzle over how it fits in 4K, with coders picking apart the technique years later.

quote.text: 2x2 is a wild resolution for a zoom-rotate-stretcher!

summary: A one-person Atari 2600 demo by Tjoppen, who did the code, graphics and music, placed third in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k11.
why: A solo VCS production that took third at Silly Venture 2k11, with its source code released for anyone curious how it was done on the 2600.

summary: A short Commodore 64 demo by Slipstream, with code by TMR, graphics by Bully The Kid and TMR, and music by Scarzix. It came 2nd in the Old School Demo compo at Sundown 2015.
why: Sceners single out Scarzix's music above all, along with the fresh, stylish effects. One called it the best $d016 noise glitch yet on the C64 and praised the line-colour-masking face.

quote.text: Stylish, fresh, solid, powerful. Excellent stuff!

summary: A Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by The Electronic Knights (TÉK), placed second in the 8-bit demo compo at Oxyron Party 2008.
why: A second place in a mixed 8-bit demo competition is a solid showing for a C16/Plus 4 production against other machines.

summary: Panda Design's C64 demo built around a social-media theme, which won the Combined Demo compo at Gerp 2016. Hires graphics, a twisting mobile phone part and a snake part run to a single soundtrack.
why: Sceners praise its coherent theme and pacing, the stylish hires graphics and the music, and welcome its social commentary. Several say it held their attention to the end.

quote.text: what i miss in contemporary c64 scene productions is exactly THIS - a social commentary, a non-mathematical feeling, a human factor.

summary: A 1K intro for the Vectrex by Realm Of Illusion, a vector-drawn Christmas tree with a "Happy New Year" message, which won the LowEnd Demo compo at DiHalt 2023.
why: A compo winner squeezed into a single kilobyte on the vector-display Vectrex, and the source is available for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: Camelot's C64 intro from X 2010, where it placed 8th in the demo compo. Code and graphics by Cruzer, music by Linus: a colourful plasma part with palm trees and fruit, plus text pages and greetings.
why: Presented as a part too lame for their coming demo, yet sceners rate its smooth, colourful 2x2-style plasma among the best on the C64. Linus's Hawaiian-flavoured tune gets plenty of praise too, and Cruzer later wrote a white paper explaining the plasma.

quote.text: Everything so smooth and colorful. A short but great gem.

summary: A small C64 plasma demo by Undone, with code and music by Encore, that came 2nd in the demo compo at Gubbdata 2013. A run of plasmas drawn in tiny triangle patterns.
why: Sceners praise the music as much as the visuals and call the plasmas original and fresh. Encore credits late pattern variations on the colour RAM routine, using extended colour mode, for their extra depth.

quote.text: really great, coolest c64 plasma i've seen i reckon. tiny triangles make it rule!

summary: An NES demo by Otomata Labs, with code by AArt1256 and Natt, graphics by Grongy and music by Nik-O. It took third place in the Oldskool Demo competition at Revision 2025.
why: A podium finish in a strong Revision oldskool compo, and it is on the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist, which marks it as one of the year's notable releases.

summary: Onslaught's Vectrex demo, coded by Razdee and Elder0010 with music by MAT64, which came second in the Retro/alternative intro/demo compo at Flashparty 2020.
why: A rare demo for the vector-display Vectrex from a group better known on the C64, placed second at Flashparty 2020. The video is real hardware footage of the glowing screen.

summary: Xanth F/X's 1986 Atari 8-bit demo, coded and designed by Michael Park: the Atari Fuji logo spins and bounces over a red-and-white checkerboard, captioned "FujiBoink!".
why: One of the early Atari 8-bit demos, from 1986. It is widely known as Atari's answer to the Amiga's famous bouncing Boing Ball demo.

summary: Brainwave's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2001, with code by Vivid, music by Megus, graphics by Pheel and design by Tigrr.
why: A compo winner at one of the main Russian Spectrum parties. It is tagged for stellar mode and Spectrum multicolour, both ways of getting more colour out of the machine than its usual attribute limits allow.

summary: Hack n' Trade's PETSCII demo for the C64, placed 6th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2013: an animated pirate story by acidT*rroreast, coded by Mathman with music by Goto80.
why: Sceners single out its direction and tight sync between Goto80's music and the animation, along with its humour and glitchy, deliberately uncomfortable feel. Some found the flicker irritating, though others see it as part of the music.

quote.text: So superb in originality and execution, makes everything else in the compo look a bit like the same.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro coded by JAC!, placed third in the Atari XL/XE 256b compo at Silly Venture 2k16.
why: A podium finish in a 256-byte compo at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, from a prod small enough to fit in a couple of lines of hex.

summary: Atlantis's C64 demo, second in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2017 Summer, with code by Dr. Science and others, graphics by Diamond Design and FatFrost, and music by Ald and DivertigO.
why: Sceners called it Atlantis's best demo to date, praising its flow, transitions, stylish design and effects that aren't trivial to code. Diamond Design's graphics drew particular mention.

quote.text: This is an awesome demo with nice effects, good graphics, coherent theme and cozy beats.

summary: Smash Designs and The Starforce's C64 demo, coded and drawn by AEG with music by SoNiC, which came third in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2007.
why: Divided opinion at release over polish and recycled effects, but sceners praise the soundtrack, AEG's solid code and the way effects are embedded into the graphics.

quote.text: All together it went wonderfully and the soundtrack is one of the best ones out there.

summary: Chaos is a demo for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Absence And Wilds, released in February 2005.
why: A joint production between two groups on the Plus/4, a less-travelled Commodore machine. It's well regarded on Pouët, where nobody has voted it down.

summary: Camelot's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2004: a press-space run of code-first parts by Cruzer, with music from DRAX, Fanta and Jeff.
why: A deliberately oldskool, effects-over-design demo. Sceners single out the diagonal raster bars and the closing 16-colour hires plasma, which some watched for half an hour.
highlights: music by DRAX, Fanta and Jeff

quote.text: despite its simpleness (codewise) the tilted rasters are fucking spectacular, and so well executed it would be hard to top it. Another highlight is the last plasma part.

summary: A 4K intro for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Resource and Logicoma, coded by Edhellon and Oswald with music by H0ffman and graphics by Poison. It won the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2023.
why: A compo winner at Revision 2023, one of the bigger stages for size-limited oldskool work, and a rare chance to see the Plus 4 in a 4K intro.

summary: Hokuto Force's C64 conversion of the opening cutscene from Another World, coded and drawn by Majikeyric with music by Uctumi. It won the Retro Demo compo at Flashparty 2019.
why: Sceners praise how faithfully the game's famous intro cinematic comes across as full-frame animation on the C64, with the final part where the hero climbs out of the water singled out.
highlights: hero climbing out of the water

quote.text: impressive work guyz!!! what a beautiful full-frame animation.

summary: Fairlight and Genesis Project's C64 demo built around ghostbyte tricks, coded by Trident with graphics by Pal, The Sarge and Redcrab and music by Fegolhuzz. It won the demo compo at Fjälldata 2024.
why: Coders single out hires graphics on the borders that seem to cross every boundary, done with ghostbytes, a field they thought was fully explored. Sceners also praise the soundtrack, the rain scene and the Panoramic tribute.

quote.text: Wow. What a demo. Makes it feel like the c64 never had any borders. Mad coding skills. Fresh ideas.

summary: Unbound is an Atari Lynx demo by New Generation that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Xenium 2025. Code is by Solo and Laoo, graphics by Tiger, kris3d and AquaSixio, and music by ZoltarX and Loop.
why: It won its compo at Xenium 2025 and was nominated for Best production at ZBOWiD 2026. Demos on the Atari Lynx are rare, which makes this a notable recent example for the handheld.
highlights: shaded cubes over a detailed picture

summary: Camelot's 16K C64 intro, coded and drawn by Cruzer with music by Homo Sidiens, which came second in the Intro category at Intro Creation Competition 2018. A cloud-textured Camelot logo sits between scrollers running in the top and bottom borders.
why: Sceners single out the cloud effect in the logo and the border scrollers, which several call impossible. Commenters describe it as demo material in intro size.

quote.text: That is top notch trickery stuff. Demo material in intro size. Both fx are amazing, don't understand the clouds fx yet.
